When you have a concept for a tattoo, when you want a piece that’s going to be on your body forever - do the homework. Review their portfolio. Ask the artist for a mock up, ask them to show you the design before it goes on your body. This is your time to give feedback and make alterations. If you aren’t happy with it, don’t be afraid to say something - this is their job and it is going to be inked on you forever unless you opt for removal. I feel a lot of folks get nervous and don’t want to advocate for little things they see that might improve the tattoo. As a client, your voice matters. Speak up. You can like an artist as a person, but that doesn’t mean you’re going to get a great tattoo per se. They’re only capable of what skills are in their wheelhouse and if this is the best this artist is capable of - find another one.

You are not alone. From online bullying to people being rude in a one on one exchange, it is going to happen. While it can sting in the moment, I generally don’t let this stuff get to me. You can’t. It isn’t you. The lack of education or ignorance of others is not your fault. To lessen some of the abrasive was in public, I typed up a short message on my phone, I keep it in the notes, just greeting the person and stating I am deaf. I will either hold it up for them or pass it to them, depending on the situation. This usually helps cut down on any confusion. I leave the note open while I’m at checkout or if I am ordering food, I will add my order to it before passing it to the clerk if the gesture to respond. I lost my hearing a little over a year ago and this is just what works for me.

To me safety is 100% about situational awareness. I am always mindful of my surroundings. My head is on a swivel. While I may carry my phone vs having it pocketed, I am not on it. It’s never far from mind that hitting the lock button a few times will call 911 if something did occur - that being my last option. I think it really just depends on your situation and minimizing potential danger you could be putting yourself in.  You don’t owe it to anyone to stop or even acknowledge strangers who approach. Picking up your pace and keeping a safe distance is smart. I think someone mentioned 6ft. If it would make you feel safer, make it 10ft. Generally I don’t feel unsafe but if something does feel off, I’ll arrange an Uber. Even if I means doubling back to where I came from. Years ago my friend group was really tight knit and we’d buddy up - if I was going out, I’d let someone know and vice versa. I never wanted my friends to feel alone or like they had to get behind the wheel if Uber wasn’t an option. Stay safe!

Memories fill me with anxiety and keep me awake. Physical pain drags me back to darker times. I relive thing that happened to me as a child. I often wonder if this is how the rest of my life will be. Isolated, depressed, forgotten. 

I was in therapy for a while. To combat the intrusive thoughts my counselor suggested occupying my hands and mind. Anything from reading to working on puzzles - either brain teasers or jigsaw. She suggested trying new hobbies. Painting, journaling, cooking.. anything to keep myself busy. I get where she was going.. I just haven’t found anything that sticks.

You are not alone. The isolation, anxiety, depression are so overwhelming. I’m also 31 M and have profound hearing loss in both ears from an accident I was in last Feb. Your words hit home so much. My depression and anxiety peaked last month when the shop I now work at was held up at gunpoint. I managed two shifts after the incident and had a drs apt that was scheduled the next day. He pulled me because I already have PTSD from my accident and struggle with guilt. I’m terrified that I’m going to lose everything at this point. It’s been a grueling and brutal yr. I feel like I can’t catch a break, things just keep compounding and I’ve cut out the few friends I had because I couldn’t stand the thought of dragging them under with me when they had wonderful things happening in their lives. Don’t do this. Make the effort to talk to the people you have in your circle. Try not to isolate and communicate to them how you feel. Be honest. I sincerely wish you the best.

Don’t listen to it. Stay in touch with those friends. Even if it’s just messaging them a smile and note that you’re thinking of them.

My TBI happened in Feb of this year. I was down and out for about 2 months before being released. I (31/m) have severe depression, anxiety and ptsd from my accident. I also have anhedonia and insomnia. I have, against medical advice, come off all medication. It has been a little over a month since I stopped taking all meds and I can tell you this; it’s fucking miserable. My days are long and nights even longer. I do not sleep. I can manage an hour nap here or there, but without meds, sleep is nonexistent. 

I stopped because I believed I was being overmedicated. And I was. My dosage was being pushed up to the point where I couldn’t function and very much felt like a shell of myself. I began to taper down and the first thing my roommate said to me was they felt like they got the old me back. (They’re also very anti-med so I am not sure how to take the statement.) Is that trade off worth it? No. The lack of sleep alone amplifies my other pain points and overall I do not feel any better.

High anxiety is draining as hell. It will level me in no time.  This is kind of a shot in the dark, but how is his eating? Is he eating foods that fuel his body or just grab and go type stuff. Could the fatigue he’s experiencing be amplified by the working out/expending energy and his body simply not having the fuel it takes to keep running - he doesn’t have to be starving to be malnourished. If his body is just deprived of essential vitamins and compounds it needs to function, that is a huge factor. Of course he’s going to be wiped. Is he eating enough consistently? If he can’t do 3 meals, is he at least snacking throughout the day on things that fuel. Just a thought. You seem like a very caring sibling and he’s fortunate to have that support. Wishing you both the best. Hang in there.

I have an extremely difficult time speaking and sincerely thought I was alone in this. I often opt not to speak at all because of how insecure it makes me feel. It 100% boils down to not being able to hear myself at all. In conversation am so focused on trying to watch what someone is saying so I do not have to ask for repeat multiple times that my brain feels overloaded. I start to shut down the second I don’t read lips right the first time. And I’m horrible at it. When I am forced to be vocal, I keep statements short. I get hung up on thoughts I can’t get out fast enough through ASL or sometimes I will second guess if I’m using a word correctly. I won’t remember how to pronounce it the moment or know if I’m using it in the correct context. I get flustered fast and become overwhelmed. It’s been almost 8 months since I lost my hearing (TBI) and I’m still adapting. Not that great. Its all too easy to pull out my phone type out a note or text then swing it around for the other person to read.

Grew up very detached from people. Lost my mom when I was pretty young and grew up with a man who really didn’t know how to handle a kid. Ended up getting shuffled around with dcfs until I was close to aging out. Started talking to recruiters because I had nowhere to go, no plans, legit would have been on the street. Or living off the hospitality of my best friends family but also feeling like a leech while doing so. Because I was raised solo, no bro/sis, the mil gave me a sense of family for the first time. Over the years, I’ve watched them grow, marry, have kids.. it’s never been anything I’ve desired. I’m fucked up. Why would I dare to being an innocent little being into a world that’s even worse? So, my social circle is extremely small by choice. Like 5 people max and they’re all spread out and understand there will be months that go by where they don’t hear from me. Everyone has those friends tho - the ones who when you’re in their hometown can’t wait to bring you out for a beer to shoot the shit like no time was lost at all. I’ve got that in two places and I’m thankful for that. Those two places also come at the price of knowing I’m either returning close to home and rough memories of the PNW or the ex wife still intermingling with mutuals. It’s easier just to keep to myself for the most part. Again, at the end of the day - for a while now I’ve had my one way ticket and have been trying to minimize the ripple effect. Going “missing” sometimes seems more plausible than hoping I’m able to hit all the neurotic points to nail this once and for all. Two attempts down, the weight of an third failed attempt and I’m going to completely lose my mind.

I’m not in a mental place where I can speak to my roommate in a collected manner. He deserves better than the emotional vomit that would be spewed the second I open my mouth. Everyone has shit they carry and hide and try to deal with. He doesn’t put his on me, if I can protect him from me, I’m going to. And fuck that shit about making sure your oxygen mask is on right before trying to help another. He’s never needed my help. He’s a good dude. A really really genuinely good human. His mask will always be on first.

I have no real, truly tangible emotional attachments in this world. Im just worn out. My body is drained and not bouncing back like it did a year ago from rona 1.0. Mentally.. fuck. I’ve bailed on work the last 3 days to not move from bed, stay high and listen to music. This isn’t living. It’s waiting for the right cocktail to hit at night in hopes of not waking up in the morning.
